description: The Mint Spring house, identified in the title as the birthplace of the artist's "Nana," is shown as a pale yellow two-story farmhouse with a vine-draped wraparound porch set behind a white picket fence. A woman in a long red dress and a small child stand at the gate, adding a quiet period feel. Autumn trees, a small outbuilding and a broad dirt road frame the house under a bright, cloud-filled sky. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

Gretchen Link depicts the S.W. Link house, a symmetrical two-story red brick farmhouse with end chimneys and green shutters, seen across weathered wooden fences and an open gate. Two small figures stand in the columned doorway, and a dirt path leads the eye toward them. Bare trees, pale hills and outbuildings behind the house suggest a rural setting in late fall or winter. The title links the house to the Link family; it is signed "G Link" at lower left.

A rooster in rich orange, gold and teal plumage stands in profile beside two hens, one of which drinks from a shallow blue dish, in front of a shadowed barn doorway. The sunlit, sandy ground and loosely brushed walls give the scene a warm, quiet farmyard mood. Signed and dated "G Link 82" below center, placing the painting in 1982.

Gretchen Link's head-and-shoulders portrait of an older woman, titled "Grandmother Helmick," shows her with soft white hair, blue eyes and a gentle smile. She wears a pale blue dress with a broad collar, a pearl necklace and earring, and a small floral brooch. The figure is modeled in soft, smooth strokes against a loosely brushed background that shifts from cool grey to warm brown. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A golden rooster stands at the center of this barnyard scene, with a white hen and a brown hen with chicks gathered at a barn door behind him and two more chicks crossing the foreground. At left, a small weathered coop with an arched opening sits before a bank of pink hollyhock-like flowers. The warm, sunlit palette and busy grouping of birds give the painting a homey, pastoral feel. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

This pet portrait shows Barclay, a small shaggy dog with curly cream and tan fur, facing the viewer with tongue out and a blue ribbon tied at the neck. The fur is built up in lively, textured strokes that stand out against a dark brown and grey background. The title appears to give the dog's name. A faint "G Link" signature is at lower left.

Large begonia-like leaves fill this watercolor, their rosy pink and deep red centers edged in scalloped yellow-green and marked by dark blue veins. The leaves are set against a loose, mottled blue-grey wash that lets the color of the foliage stand out. Signed and dated "G Link 88" in blue at lower right, placing the work in 1988.

Drawn in black marker, an open-sided wooden pavilion stands on posts above the dunes, with beachgoers seated in deck chairs as dark silhouettes beneath its flat roof. Brisk hatching marks the shadow on the sand, while dune grass and a few loose strokes for footprints leave much of the paper open. The work is signed "G Link Ju 77," most likely June or July 1977, and "Nagshead" is penciled below, placing the scene at Nags Head on the North Carolina Outer Banks.

In this still life, a woven basket with a tall arched handle holds leafy greens and an ear of corn, with two yellow crookneck squash and a red tomato on the table before it. The garden produce is set against a split background of golden yellow and red brick, with the vegetables painted in thick, direct strokes. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A Raggedy Ann doll with red yarn hair and a blue dress sits beside a dark brown teddy bear in a red plaid scarf, the two sharing a small cream-colored rocking chair. The paint is applied thickly, and the bold orange-red and green background and multicolored floor give the picture a vivid, playful look. No signature is visible.

A head-and-shoulders portrait of a smiling teenage boy, identified by the title as Lee Hunter, set against a soft blue-gray ground. Gretchen Link models the face with warm, blended flesh tones and renders the thick dark hair and teal polo shirt in looser, broader strokes. The sitter meets the viewer directly with a relaxed, closed-mouth smile. The work is signed "G Link" at lower left and is undated.

A drawing of the house at 35 Woodland Drive, a two-story brick residence with shutters, a pedimented front door and a one-story wing with a covered porch. Gretchen Link outlines the building and the surrounding trees and shrubs in fine pen line, adding only light touches of colored pencil, so that much of the cream paper remains bare. The curved driveway and foundation plantings frame the house in a home-portrait manner. It is inscribed "May 80" and signed "G Link" at lower right.

A seated woman in a brimmed hat, red jacket and apron works on a coiled sweetgrass basket in her lap, surrounded by finished baskets on the ground and hanging from a rough wooden rack. The figure and baskets are painted in warm golds, reds and blues against largely untouched paper, giving the scene a light, open feel. Sweetgrass basket weaving is a Gullah craft closely associated with the Charleston area, which the inscription "Charlston '83" (as spelled) at lower right names. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A single salmon-pink amaryllis bloom fills the center of this watercolor, its petals shaded in coral with a pale yellow-green throat and yellow-tipped stamens. Long strap-like leaves fan out around it, and a bud and a fainter second bloom appear at the top and right. The background is a loose, soft wash of yellow, green and blue that fades into bare paper at the edges. Signed "G Link" below the flower; undated.

A tabletop still life in pastel with a deep blue bowl of apples and yellow fruit, a loose green apple, a tall blue-green vase and a dark pitcher, all set on a rumpled white cloth with thin red stripes. Gretchen Link builds the forms with visible hatched strokes, and the background is worked in ochre, rust and blue. The strong blues of the bowl and vase anchor the composition. Signed "G Link" with the date "'90" at lower left.

The gable end of a small ochre stucco church with a rust-red roof and a belfry topped by a wooden cross, painted in loose watercolor washes under a bright blue, cloud-streaked sky. A bare forked tree trunk stands against the wall, and dark chickens peck in the shaded dirt yard below. The adobe-style construction suggests the American Southwest or a similar setting, though no place is named on the work. Signed "G Link" at lower right; undated.

A village scene of whitewashed houses with clay-tile roofs grouped around a sunny, sandy yard. Laundry in reds and oranges hangs along a wall at left, and a woman, a small child and a figure in dark clothing stand near an arched passage at center. Chickens, including a red rooster and a gray hen, occupy the foreground, adding to the everyday rural character. The location is not identified; the work is signed "G Link" at left and is undated.

A brick house on Selma Boulevard, as the title records, shown deep in snow under a gray winter sky. The steep snow-laden roof, tall chimney and arched entry dominate the composition, with a second brick gable and a snow-covered car at left and bare, snow-dusted trees in the yard. Cool blue-gray shadows in the snow contrast with the warm red of the brick. Signed "G Link" at lower left; undated.

A late-autumn farm scene with a red barn, a smaller outbuilding and a white farmhouse on a grassy rise above a still pond. Golden hills roll away to the right, and the pond in the foreground reflects the barn and sky among rust-colored brush and dried wildflowers. The sky is painted with billowing white clouds over soft blue. The farm is not identified; signed "G Link" at lower right and undated.

A red popcorn wagon with yellow spoked wheels and gold trim draws customers on a broad, tree-lined path, with a domed building resembling the United States Capitol in the distance, consistent with the Washington, D.C. setting given in the title. Two customers stand at the counter while other pedestrians, including an adult with a small child, stroll toward the dome. Pigeons feed in the foreground and one perches on the wagon roof. Signed "G Link" at lower right, with a faint penciled "Lunch" along the bottom edge that may be an intended title.

A watercolor seaside view of two weathered houses set among dunes, a pale yellow house with a red roof and rooftop cupola at left and a dark grey shingled cottage at right. A strip of ocean shows between them under a heavy, stormy sky. Loose washes of dune grass, shrubs and small red and yellow wildflowers fill the foreground. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A watercolor still life of a dense bouquet of primroses in yellow, red, purple and pink, set in a worn metal tin. Partial lettering on the tin reads "IRISH OAT...", suggesting a reused oatmeal container. The painted area floats on white paper, the flowers framed by a loose blue and violet wash. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A brightly colored pastel still life of a red geranium in a blue pot, with a red apple, a green pear and a large orange lined up in front on a pale blue surface. The vivid yellow background and visible, hatched pastel strokes give the work a warm, energetic feel. Signed "G Link" and dated "90" at lower left, one of several pastel still lifes from 1990.

A pastel still life of a bunch of purple grapes with a leaf and curling tendrils, a red apple, a pear and an orange, grouped beside a brown and cream stoneware jug. The arrangement sits on a white cloth over a wooden table, with a blue drape behind the jug against a pale yellow wall. Signed "G Link" and dated "90" at lower right, it belongs with other pastel still lifes from 1990.

A pastel still life of two brown stoneware vessels at the back with a green bell pepper and a curved yellow fruit, apparently a banana, in front. At right a brown bowl holds an apple, an orange and red grapes spilling over its rim. The objects rest on a white cloth with strong blue shadows against a pale yellow and peach ground. Signed "G Link" and dated "90" at lower right, part of a group of 1990 pastel still lifes.

An oil painting of a small stone church seen from a front corner, with steep grey roofs, a large round-arched entry porch and a small belfry above the ridge. Ivy climbs the wall beside the porch, and dark trees stand behind. The handling is loose and broadly brushed in a muted palette of greys and ochres. The church is not identified, and no signature is visible.

An oil head-and-shoulders study of a short-haired person in three-quarter view, gazing to the left with a serious expression. It is painted in a restricted palette of browns, tans and greys against a loosely brushed warm background. The title identifies it as a portrait from an art class in 1992, and the sitter is not named. Signed "G Link" in white at lower left.

A pastel on tan paper of an open, columned white cupola with a bell-shaped roof and ornamental finial, viewed from rooftop level. Beyond it a green valley scattered with small houses stretches toward low blue mountains, with a water tower on the horizon at left. The sky is built up in streaked, hatched strokes of blue and white. Signed "G Link" and dated "78" at lower right.

A pen drawing tinted with colored pencil of a two-story red brick house with many-paned windows, a chimney and a columned front porch over a paneled double door. A large tree frames the left side, its branches reaching across the roof, and daylilies grow along the foundation. The careful line work gives a clear account of the building. Signed "G Link" and dated "May '82" at lower right, it is a companion to the Highland Church drawing of the same month.

A brown ink drawing of a rural valley scene with a small clapboard church with a square belfry and slender spire at right. A weathered barn, a shed and a leaning utility pole stand at left, with split-rail and board fences in the foreground and mountain ridges beyond. The handling is quick and linear, with a few birds sketched in the sky. Signed "G Link" and dated "May '82" at lower right, a companion to the Highland House drawing of the same month.

A detailed brown-ink drawing of the den at 35 Woodland Dr, centered on a broad masonry fireplace with a kettle hung from an iron crane over the logs. The mantel holds a display of pewter-like plates, pitchers and a large charger, with dried corn and hanging utensils at either end. Bookshelves, a wingback chair and a child's rocking chair frame the hearth, giving the room a lived-in, colonial-revival character. Signed and dated "G Link Feb '80" at lower left.

An abstracted city skyline in which towers dissolve into soft, streaked vertical strokes of cream, grey and blue under a hazy sky. Pale buildings at center catch the light while darker forms crowd around them, and small horizontal dashes stand in for windows. The blurred handling gives the scene an atmospheric, almost misty quality, with a few touches of red and ochre near the base. Signed "G Link" at lower right; undated.

An oil pastel still life of a potted poinsettia, its bright green leaves and red bracts set against a deep blue and violet ground worked in vigorous, visible strokes. An orange and a green apple rest in front of the green pot on a pale tabletop, their rounded forms balancing the jagged foliage above. The strong color contrasts give the piece a lively, seasonal feel. Signed "G Link" and dated '90 at lower left.

A floral still life of chrysanthemum-like blooms in orange, golden yellow and white, mixed with sprays of rust-colored foliage in a white footed bowl on a plate. A cluster of green grapes lies beside the bowl at lower left. Soft, blended brushwork and a muted olive and ochre background give the arrangement a warm, autumnal tone. Signed "G Link" at lower left; undated.

A pastel garden view of a small red brick outbuilding with a steep, dark pyramidal roof, half hidden among rounded green shrubs. Arching tree branches frame the top of the scene and a tall evergreen trunk rises at right beside a white fence. The building is drawn with loose, layered strokes of green and blue that emphasize dappled light and shade on the lawn. Unsigned and undated.

A watercolor view looking out through a multi-paned kitchen window at a rustic homestead: a weathered log cabin with a flower box, a small outhouse and a split-rail fence, with a yellow field, wooded hills and blue mountains beyond. Colored glass bottles and a jug stand on the sill in the foreground, setting the interior against the landscape outside. The title names the place as Highland, and the scene suggests a mountain setting. Unsigned and undated.

A loose watercolor sketch of the side of a house, where a blue window under a dark roof is overgrown by twisting vine stems with orange and yellow autumn leaves. Green shrubs anchor the base and a small orange-leaved tree stands at right. Washes are left open and run together, giving the study a quick, spontaneous feel within its ruled pencil border. A circled "6" at lower left and a "lgpst000037" label suggest it belongs to a numbered series with Front Gate.

A watercolor of a weathered grey board gate with a scalloped top, set in a rail fence beside a tall lamp post with a lantern. A red brick path leads up to the gate, a small leafy tree grows at left, and a bed of red, orange, yellow and blue flowers, including a tall blue spike, blooms at right. Soft, pale green washes fill the background within a ruled pencil border. A circled "5" at lower left and a "lgpst000038" label suggest it belongs to a numbered series with Side Window.

A watercolor vignette of a grey board barn with tan shingled roofs standing behind a wooden rail fence. A small dark figure stands near the building beside a tall, slender tree, and soft washes of green, blue-grey and gold suggest surrounding trees, with a yellow-orange tree hinting at autumn. Orange flowers bloom in the foreground, and the edges fade into the bare paper. Signed "G Link" at lower left; undated.

A pen drawing in brown marker, lightly shaded with blue and pink colored pencil, of a tall water tower rising above tiled rooftops, chimneys and trees, with houses climbing a hillside beyond. The line work is quick and sketch-like, giving a sense of a travel drawing made on the spot. The inscription at lower right reads "G Link, Hotel Abalia, Albufeara '79, Portugal," apparently referring to the town of Albufeira in the Algarve, dated 1979.

A garden path curves through deep flower borders toward a white birdbath set before a cluster of rounded trees, with an open field and blue hills beyond. Tall blue delphinium spikes frame the scene, set off by red, yellow and orange blooms. The flowers are built up in loose, layered dabs of color, while the sky and distant hills are handled in soft, bleeding washes. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A head-and-shoulders portrait, identified by its title as Pat Hunter, shows a smiling woman with short dark hair and large dark sunglasses. She wears a white turtleneck under a red sweater with a beaded necklace. The figure is modeled with some care, while the background is a loose blue-grey and tan wash that fades into bare paper. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A white lighthouse and a gabled keeper's house stand on a stone breakwater in this harbor scene, with more white houses and trees along the far shore. A tall-masted sailboat and a small motorboat ride on the blue water at right, and a lone figure in a red shirt fishes from the rocky shore in the foreground. The painting is handled in clear, fairly detailed washes with lively water. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A large pale building with a windowed rooftop cupola and a columned porch is half hidden behind trees in golden and rust autumn foliage, with two small figures on the walk in front. The trees and sky are painted in loose, warm washes, and a stone wall is lightly sketched along the bottom edge. The building is on the campus of Mary Baldwin University in Staunton, Virginia. No signature is visible.

A derelict wooden fishing boat with a broken wheelhouse and two bare masts sits at the water's edge beside a sagging pier, with pale hills across the bay. The palette is restrained to browns, greys and cream, and the still water reflects the pilings, giving the scene a quiet, faded mood. The stained, patched hull is described in some detail against the softer background. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A white arbor heavy with pink climbing roses spans stone steps that lead along a curving path toward a white rail fence, with flower beds on either side and dark trees behind. The work is painted on unstretched canvas, and the lower third is left bare below a loosely brushed lawn, so it appears unfinished. Signed "G Link" at lower left of the painted area.

A woman in a long white dress and flowered hat walks hand in hand with a small child in white along a dirt path toward a group of buildings. These include a large round white structure with a rust-red roof, a pointed red-roofed pavilion and a long arcaded building with a blue-green roof, set among hedges and trees beneath blue mountains. The clothing suggests a period or historical setting, though the location is not identified. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

Weathered farm buildings, including a grey barn with a red roof, a tall board shed and a small red-roofed house, stand on a hilltop beneath a streaked grey sky. A bare, pale-barked tree with a few remaining leaves rises in the foreground over a brown and ochre slope dotted with brush and fence posts. The muted palette and brisk, visible brushwork convey a cold, late-season day. No signature is visible.

A low glass bowl of pansies in yellow, white, deep purple and maroon sits on a wooden table, with two cut blossoms lying beside it. The background shifts from near black at left to pale grey-green at right, setting off the bright flowers. The blossoms are painted with soft, broad strokes that keep their dark face markings. Signed "Gretchen Link" in full at lower right.

A tall copper coffee pot stands among vegetables arranged on a white cloth: an onion and a dark eggplant at left, a head of cauliflower at center, red tomatoes, mushrooms, a bunch of carrots and a green vegetable at right. The objects are set against a dark brown ground in a traditional still-life arrangement. The canvas is unstretched, with tack holes along its edges, and is faintly signed "G Link" at lower left.

An intimate pastel, titled for Raymond Link and Lee Hunter, shows a man from behind as he sits in a webbed aluminum lawn chair with a small child in a white cap resting on his shoulder. Quick, open strokes of green and yellow on brown paper suggest a birch and dense foliage around them, leaving the toned paper to carry much of the scene. The work is signed and dated "G Link 78" at lower left.

Two butterflies occupy opposite ends of a tall, narrow pastel on toned paper: an orange butterfly with white-spotted black borders in profile at the top, and a yellow swallowtail feeding on pale pink blossoms at the bottom. A softly blended green and blue ground fills the space between them. Signed "G Link" at lower left with a date read as 1977, though it could possibly be 1979.

A small oil view of the Hilton Head lighthouse, its red and white bands standing beside a white house at the edge of a harbor. Docks and a curving walkway reach out over blue water toward a distant sailboat, with a red flag and green trees at right. The scene is painted as a rectangle in the center of a larger piece of unprimed canvas, leaving a wide bare border around the image. The work is undated and unsigned on its face.

A breezy watercolor of the beach at Nags Head, seen from the dunes past a red scalloped umbrella, beach chairs and a tall clump of sea oats. Along the shore small figures fish in the surf beneath a pale sky with gulls, and a second umbrella sits farther down the beach. The light washes leave much of the sand as bare paper. Signed "G Link" in orange, with "'94" and "Nags Head" written in pencil in the lower margin.

A botanical study in pen and watercolor of a single tiger lily stem running the full height of a tall, narrow sheet. Three open blooms with recurved, dark-spotted orange petals and long stamens are drawn with careful line, while closed buds hang near the top and slender leaves line the stem. A pale yellow wash glows behind the center. Signed and dated "G Link 1978" at lower right.

Looking up at a round red brick tower in Staunton, Virginia, this watercolor follows the turret from its arched windows and small plaque past a bracketed cornice to a steep conical roof of grey scalloped shingles. Soft blue washes and white clouds fill the sky, and the adjoining building is only faintly suggested. The sheet carries no visible signature or date.

A large weeping willow spreads its yellow-green branches over a small stone-edged island at the duck pond in Gypsy Hill Park, Staunton, Virginia. Small red brick structures sit beneath the tree, and two ducks swim in the blue water in the foreground. The loose, layered washes give the willow a soft, cascading quality. Signed "G Link '86" at lower left.

A ladder-back chair with a golden rush seat, seen from a low angle, casts a blue shadow against a loosely washed wall. At lower right a rounded tan and brown form appears to be a cat curled up asleep beside the chair. The simple domestic subject is handled in broad, fluid washes, and the sheet appears to have come from a spiral-bound pad. Signed "G Link" at lower right.

The view from a covered porch frames the ocean through white turned posts and a corner railing, with a green-painted floor and ceiling in the foreground. Beyond the railing, golden dune grass and dark shrubs lead down to a pale beach and a blue-grey sea under a cloudy sky, with a dark headland at right. The location is not identified. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A street scene of tightly grouped buildings painted in bold red, blue, yellow and green, some clad in corrugated siding and fitted with balconies, shutters and rooftop antennas. An ornate street lamp and a small kiosk with a striped awning stand at the edges of a grey street where a crowd of small, dark-clothed figures walks. The location is not named on the work. Signed "G Link" at lower left, on Arches paper.

A quick outline sketch in light brown pencil of the harbor at Woods Hole, Massachusetts, with small sailboats and a cabin boat riding at their moorings in the foreground. A long vessel lies at a dock beside two sheds, and a large house stands on a point of land against open water. The drawing is loose and economical, with squiggled lines suggesting reflections, and the place name "woodshole" is written near the bottom edge.

Gretchen Link paints an abandoned board farmhouse on a dry, tan hillside, its patchwork metal roof rusted to reds and browns and its porch sagging on thin posts. A line of fence posts climbs the slope behind, and tufts of green grass break up the ochre foreground under a soft blue-grey sky. Soft, translucent washes give the scene a quiet, weathered mood. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A tall stand of bearded irises in peach, rose, lavender and deep purple, with blooms and tight buds rising at different heights among upright sword-shaped leaves. The artist sets the flowers against loose washes, warm yellow behind the upper blooms and cool blue-grey at the right, and leaves the lower part of the sheet largely open. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A still life of a mixed bouquet of dark purple tulips, mauve rose-like blooms, peach flowers, white clusters and tall spikes of pale pink stock in a fluted white vase decorated with a small floral spray. The vase stands on a dark polished table that mirrors it, and the bouquet throws a soft shadow onto the pale green wall behind. The painting is signed "Gretchen Link" with the date '45 at lower left.

A still life of a worn brown boot, a yellow jug holding drooping olive-brown leaves around a dark red seed cluster, and a dark blue bottle lying on its side. The objects rest on rumpled yellow-green cloth against a pale blue-grey and ochre background. Thin, washy paint and loose, sketch-like handling give the piece the feel of a study.

The small red board-and-batten railway station at Fort Defiance, Virginia, shown disused, with weeds, shrubs and tall grasses growing up around its low platform. Its wide hipped roof with ornamental ridge ends, brick chimney and bay window are set against dark green trees and blue mountains under a cloudy sky, and a utility pole stands at the left. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A portrait of Pat Hunter at Nags Head, North Carolina, standing on a sandy path and smiling at the viewer in a yellow straw hat and a long blue button-front dress. A weathered slat sand fence curves along the dune behind her and casts striped shadows across the sand, with dune grass above and a strip of blue ocean at the left. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A pastel still life of a bunch of blue-black grapes lying in front of a rounded copper pot, with golden-green grapes, vine leaves and a curling tendril to the left and a few loose grapes on the dark tabletop. Soft blending gives the fruit a gentle sheen against the grey background. The sheet shows torn and stained edges. Signed "Gretchen Link" at lower left.

An interior still life of baskets stacked on a dark cabinet: a small handled basket, a large lidded wicker hamper and a grey splint basket with a tall arched handle, beside a pot of dried rust and pink flowers. A fringed red-and-white woven coverlet hangs over one side of the cabinet, partly covering a shelf of books. Soft grey washes surround the arrangement. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A still life of a dark pewter pitcher filled with glossy magnolia branches, set against a mottled golden-yellow wall. Beside it a footed bowl holds a banana, apples, an orange, a pear and grapes, with a pomegranate and a walnut resting on a blue-and-white checked cloth. A blue cloth draped over a chair post at the lower left adds a second cool note. Signed "G. Link" with a two-digit date at lower right.

A quiet rural scene in which a still farm pond reflects a red-roofed white barn, with a second pale barn and a full green tree at right. A slender, leaning tree frames the left side, and golden summer hills and darker wooded ridges rise beneath a soft, clouded sky. The paint is handled loosely, with broken reflections in the water. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

Gretchen Link portrays a young girl in three-quarter length, turned away and glancing back over her shoulder at the viewer. Her long strawberry-blonde hair is tied with a yellow bow, and she wears a white puff-sleeved blouse and a full blue skirt whose sheen is picked out in light strokes while holding a small posy of pink flowers. The near-black background and a hint of a red curtain give the portrait a formal, old-master feel. Signed "G Link" in red at lower right.

A pastel head-and-shoulders portrait of a small girl facing the viewer with a calm, direct gaze. Her blonde hair is parted in the center and drawn into looped braids tied with pink ribbons, and she wears a pink dress with a rounded white collar and lace trim. The figure is set against a rubbed blue-green and brown ground on tan paper that shows wear and staining at the edges. The work is signed and dated twice at lower right, "G. Link '44," placing it in 1944.

A genial watercolor genre scene of three white-haired women passing the time outside a steep-gabled, shingled cottage. One leans on a straw broom with her back to the viewer, another stands smiling with hands on hips, and a third sits in a rocking chair with sewing in her lap. Climbing pink roses, vines and yellow flowers soften the weathered grey shingles around the doorway, which carries a small sign. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

Worked in colored pastel on deep blue paper, this portrait shows a woman with a dark bob and bangs seated in profile in a wooden chair, a slight smile on her face. She wears a loose blue-green robe embroidered with yellow, red and gold motifs, and her hand rests beside a glass vase of white and yellow daisies. The blue paper is left showing through the strokes, unifying the figure and background. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A winter view over a snowbound hillside neighborhood in Staunton, Virginia. In the foreground a low brick house has a shovel propped by its door and a small orange hatchback parked out front, while dozens of red brick and yellow houses with white roofs climb the slope behind among bare trees and evergreens. The wash handling keeps the scene light and airy under a pale grey-blue sky. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

An abandoned grey-board house with a rust-streaked metal roof and brick chimney sits in a field of tall golden grass, approached past a sagging wooden gate and wire fence. A bare, twisted tree at right and a heavy cloudy sky over blue-grey hills give the scene a somber, weathered mood. Signed "G Link" at lower right with a date that appears to read 86 (1986), though the second digit is partly hidden and 88 is possible.

A still life of humble, worn objects: a battered metal bucket tipped on its side, two red apples, a gnarled piece of driftwood and a long-necked green glass bottle. The arrangement sits on a pale yellow tabletop against a loosely brushed brown and ochre background, with highlights on the bottle and dented pail. Signed "G Link" and dated 78 (1978) at lower left.

A free, gestural abstract composition of smeared dark red and maroon paint mixed with patches of mustard yellow, purple and blue, with a separate blue and purple smear at right. Thin wandering lines in green, magenta and yellow loop over and around the paint, and much of the white ground is left bare. The marks have the spontaneous look of finger painting. No signature is visible.

A tall, crenellated church tower with a round rose window and a pointed-arch doorway glows in pale pink and white against a deep blue night sky. Steps lead up to the door while the body of the church falls into shadow, and dark trees with touches of orange autumn foliage frame the tower. The brushwork is loose, and the lower edge is left sketchy and appears unfinished. No signature is visible.

A hillside cemetery looks out over open countryside in this upright oil landscape. A tall, tiered monument topped with an urn rises among weathered headstones and obelisks, while a rounded gravestone and a slender tree anchor the foreground. Beyond, sunlit yellow-green hills, a small white house and hazy blue mountains recede under a soft sky, giving the scene a quiet, pastoral mood. The brushwork is loose and the palette muted.

A young woman sits in profile on a bentwood chair, turned toward a window, with a decorated pottery jar resting in her lap. Her blue patterned headscarf, white blouse, tiered red skirt and gold bangles stand out against a cool blue-grey wall, and a bare branch is visible through the window. The mood is still and contemplative. Signed "G Link" at lower right with a date read as 1978, though 1973 is possible.

Painted in the manner of an eighteenth-century formal portrait, this oil shows an older woman seated in a gilt armchair with red upholstery, pausing in her needlework to look toward the viewer. She wears a ruffled lace cap, a white fichu and a dark gown over a full white skirt, with a blue silk workbag hanging from her arm. A dark red curtain and a nearly black background set off the figure. Signed "G Link" at lower right.

A weathered grey board chicken house with a patched, rust-colored roof stands on a grassy rise, with a hen, a rooster and chicks pecking in the yard. A red brick house with chimneys rises behind at right, and soft, loosely washed trees fill the background. The pencil caption below the image, "Chicken House - Walter Link Farm," identifies the place as a Link family farm. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A crowded summer garden fills this horizontal oil painting, centered on large yellow and orange lilies with arching leaves. Black-eyed Susans, red bee balm, daisies and yarrow surround them, with tall pink and lavender flower spikes rising behind. A hummingbird hovers over the red blooms at upper right against a hazy pale sky. The soft, blended handling gives the scene a warm, dreamy feel. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A small boy stands squarely on a worn base, looking seriously at the viewer, with a baseball in one hand and a leather glove on the other. His red cap, white shirt and blue jeans are set against a blue-grey wash crossed by pale lines that suggest a backstop fence, with tan dirt underfoot. The watercolor is handled with loose, fluid washes. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

Two young children, identified by the title as Anne and Lee, stand on a woodland path in a portrait that appears to borrow the look of nineteenth-century American folk portraiture. The girl wears a yellow dress with a lace collar and carries a bouquet and a basket of colored Easter eggs. The smaller boy, in a blue jacket and white trousers, holds the string of a wooden pull-toy horse. Dark trees frame a cloudy sky. Signed and dated "G Link 82" at lower left.

Gretchen Link painted a lively beach-scene border around a printed invitation to the wedding of Leslie Hoy and William L. Hunter, held on the twenty-first of July at Folly Beach, Charleston, South Carolina. Around a checkered frame with gold scrollwork, the border shows sea, boats and kites at top, with an umbrella, towel, sandals, sandcastle, beach ball, straw hat, an Adirondack chair with an American flag and a watermelon picnic around the sides and bottom. Signed "G Link" at bottom center.

Pale stone towers, crenellations and a Gothic arched window of Windsor Castle rise above tiled roofs and tall brick chimneys in this watercolor. In the foreground, a brick wall holds a planter of red tulips and blue and white flowers beside a flowering pink shrub. The view seems to be from a nearby garden or courtyard and combines architecture with flowers in light, airy washes. Signed and dated "G Link 87" at lower left.

An evening band concert in a park is painted almost entirely in deep blues, with the lit octagonal bandstand glowing at center. Inside, a conductor with a raised arm leads the musicians while an audience sits on benches in front. A large tree trunk frames the left side, and at right a street lamp lights a flowering tree beside the dark silhouettes of an adult and a small child. The scene has a warm, nostalgic, small-town mood. Signed and dated "G Link 76" at lower left.

A small pale church with a steep dark spire and a red door stands on a grassy rise, viewed from the front corner as a path climbs toward its stone steps. Soft, blended brushwork and a stormy grey sky give the scene a hushed, somewhat moody atmosphere, with misty blue trees closing in around the building and a flowering white shrub at lower right. The church is not identified. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A loose, abundant bouquet of lilies, daisies, snapdragons and small white and blue blossoms spills outward from a dark footed vase on a polished table, with a few fallen petals at its base. The palette is dominated by warm yellows and oranges set against a cool blue-grey background, and the flowers are handled with quick, feathery strokes. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A tabletop still life built around a wedge of watermelon, set on a white cloth over a blue checked one with a knife, a lemon, a peach in a yellow bowl, a glass tumbler and a large blue-banded white pitcher. The brushwork is loose and bright, and the dappled yellow-green background gives the arrangement a sunny, summery feel. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A cream-colored country house with a steep tiled roof, dormers and tall brick chimneys stands beyond a broad lawn, in a style suggesting an English manor or cottage. A dense border of blue and purple delphiniums, pink hollyhocks and daisies fills the foreground, and two small figures appear on the lawn. Tall trees and a bright, cloud-filled blue sky complete the cheerful garden scene. The house and its location are not identified.

A full-length portrait of a young child playing cowboy, in an oversized cream hat, a fleece-lined blue vest, red plaid trousers and tan boots, one hand tipping the hat brim and the other holding a small toy. A scruffy terrier sits at the child's feet looking out at the viewer, and red geraniums edge the brick walk in front of a doorway. The title and the tall, narrow format emphasize the playful pose. Signed and dated "G Link 1979" at lower left.

According to the title, this interior shows Pat Hunter at Ivy Nursery in Ivy, Virginia, though which figure represents her is not indicated. The greenhouse is crowded with color: hanging baskets of pink, red and white flowers and large ferns hang beneath an arched, sunlit roof, above benches of hydrangeas, lilies and price signs, one reading "MUMS 2.99". Shoppers browse among the plants while a woman in a blue dress, apron and cap waters with a hose at lower right. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

The stone gate pillars of the former Staunton Military Academy, each carved "SMA" and topped with a finial, frame open wrought-iron gates and a paved drive leading to a yellow columned building, with a small red brick building at left. The site is now part of the Mary Baldwin University campus in Staunton, Virginia. The scene is painted in fresh, sunny colors under a blue sky with drifting clouds. Signed and dated "G Link 77" at lower left.

A street-level view of a red brick building with arched blue-grey doors and windows, its base lined with pots and beds of red, white and blue flowers. A blonde woman in white overalls stands at left with her back to the viewer, while two children wait near the right-hand door beside a painted house number. Sunlight falling across the doorways and pavement gives the everyday scene a warm, quiet character. Signed and dated "G Link '76" at lower left.

A densely built hillside townscape in which brick and stucco buildings in red, ochre, yellow and white step down the slope toward a few parked cars. A church tower with a tall green spire rises at left, and a long white columned building with a small domed cupola crowns the hill, presumably Stuart Hall, the school named in the title. The compressed, stacked composition conveys the steep terrain of the town. Signed and dated "G Link 76" at lower right.

A massive, gnarled tree with a broad canopy of green and yellow leaves fills most of the canvas, a simple board swing hanging from one of its branches on long ropes. Beyond it a country road curves uphill past a wire fence and golden fields, with deep shade pooled on the lawn below. The thick, multicolored handling of the trunk and roots gives the tree a strong presence. Signed "G Link" at lower left.

A rainy-day view of two adjoining nineteenth-century commercial buildings, one red brick with green trim and one orange above a dark blue storefront, with the wet street mirroring their facades. The title places the scene on a wharf street across from a train depot. A utility pole and its wires cut across the left side, and a small black animal crosses the sidewalk. The loose, broken brushwork in the pavement conveys reflected light under an overcast sky. Signed and dated "G Link 76" at lower right.

A small fieldstone outbuilding with a shingled gable roof and plank door sits beneath a twisting tree whose bare limb arches over the roof. The title identifies the site as Mint Spring. Cool blues in the stone and shadow contrast with touches of gold and orange in the autumn foliage and sunlit ground, and spiky grasses fill the foreground. Signed and dated "G Link '82" at lower right.

A steep downtown street seen from above, lined with brick and white commercial buildings with awnings and shop signs, descends toward a skyline of a conical turret, a slender church spire and a large dome crowned by a statue. Pedestrians, a dog walker, parked vintage cars and a cyclist in red animate the street. The whole scene is softened by a hazy grey atmosphere that dissolves the distant buildings. Signed "G Link" at lower left; the work is undated.

A pale yellow house with a red tile roof, green shutters and window boxes spilling over with red and yellow flowers stands at the top of a stone stairway, while a dark-haired woman carries a basket of flowers up the steps below. A pencil caption at lower left identifies the subject as the house at the top of the stairs in Torremolinos, Spain. The washes are light and controlled, with careful pencil drawing beneath the color. Signed and dated "G Link 86" at lower right.

A slender red brick clock tower topped by a green onion dome rises above neighboring brick and yellow buildings on a sloping street, identified by the title as Staunton. Clock faces show on two sides of the tower. The sky is brushed in loose blue washes, and two rounded masses of green foliage frame a pale road in the foreground. The watercolor is unsigned and undated, set within a drawn pencil border.

The Staunton train station is seen from the platform, where a long curving canopy sweeps into the distance alongside double tracks that bend past a rocky embankment. Travelers with luggage and baggage carts wait under the canopy, and a lone figure with a bag walks away from the viewer in the foreground. Beyond rises a red brick building with a sign for the White Star Mill, beside grey mill structures, white silos and a tall utility pole. Signed and dated "G Link 78" at lower right.

An open stone pavilion with a shingled roof and two white-trussed gables stands among trees in full autumn color, identified by the title as being near the entrance to Gypsy Hill, a park in Staunton. Small figures stand inside the shelter and beside a white fence at left. Warm yellows and reds in the foliage set off the grey stone piers against a blue sky. Signed and dated "G Link 65" at lower left.

A curved, two-story portico with tall white columns and an iron railing projects from a yellow building, on the campus of Mary Baldwin University in Staunton, Virginia. Below the portico, arched doorways and a hanging lantern open onto a terrace furnished with wrought-iron chairs and tables, and a stone staircase climbs at left past a small red-leaved tree. Strong light on the columns contrasts with shadowed recesses under a blue sky. Signed "G Link" at lower left; the work is undated.

A quiet still life in dark, warm tones pairs a rounded blue-and-white ceramic jar holding dried, translucent seed pods and reddish twigs with a brass-tacked wooden trunk behind it. The objects rest on a pale cloth, with a strip of patterned drapery at right, and the dark brown background lets the pale pods and the glazed jar catch the light. Signed "G Link" at lower left; the work is undated.

Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century American folk portraiture, this full-length figure shows a small dark-haired child in a red off-the-shoulder dress with puffed sleeves and a lace neckline, white pantalettes and dark shoes, holding an orange tabby cat. The flat, frontal pose and plain dark grey background follow the conventions of that tradition. The child's pale, smoothly modeled face stands out against the deep red of the dress. No signature or date is visible.

Gretchen Link works in the manner of an early American folk painting, with flat perspective and simplified forms, in this harbor view on unstretched canvas. A large red house with a curving white fence stands at left, and sailing ships crowd the green harbor at right, one flying an American flag. Small dark figures dot the yard and wharf, and birds cross a pale, streaked sky. A gold-lettered caption along the bottom band reads "A View of Mr. Joshua Winsor's House."

A brown and white goat with long, drooping speckled ears reaches past a post to eat from a plate on a rough wooden table in a barn. The weathered gray boards, straw-covered floor, hanging feed sacks, and a broom beside pale crocks give a homely, everyday setting. The goat is painted with some care, while the surroundings are handled more loosely. Signed "G Link" in red at lower right.

A weathered barn sits at the end of a fenced dirt lane in this soft, hazy autumn landscape. Slender trees with gold and orange leaves stand at left, and a bank of orange flowers spills across the right foreground beneath dark, heavy trees. Gretchen Link uses loose, blended brushwork and muted color throughout, with streaks of blue-gray in the sky. Signed "G Link" in red at lower right.

Two tall pale-trunked trees in golden autumn foliage frame a quiet pond where three white swans float, one near the front and two farther back. Low blue hills line the far shore under a gray sky, and russet fallen leaves cover the banks. The framing trees and still water give the scene a calm, enclosed feeling. Signed "G Link" at lower right.

Gretchen Link's 1978 pastel shows a gray-shingled Cape Cod cottage with bright blue shutters and door, red brick chimneys, and window boxes of red flowers behind a white picket fence. A pine spreads its branches across the roof, a lamp post stands at left, and blue shadows fall across the sunlit lawn. The pastel is applied in visible, energetic strokes that let the cream paper show through. Inscribed "G Link Cape Cod 78" at lower right.

This still life is painted on a hexagonal panel of golden-tan velvet. A white opalescent compote heaped with strawberries rises at center, and a pink rose, pansies, small white and blue blossoms, and a bunch of purple grapes lie scattered around its base. The soft velvet ground gives the colors a muted glow. Faintly signed at the bottom, with a date that appears to be from the 1950s but is hard to read.

A solemn young girl with long brown hair and a large white bow stands on a wooden porch in a lace-trimmed white dress, black stockings, and lace-up boots. Beside her a blonde doll in a gray dress sits in an ornate wicker chair, and green fields and blue mountains open out beyond the railing. The costume and pose recall a turn-of-the-century photograph portrait. The word "MOTHER" is lettered faintly on the porch floor, and the painting is signed "G Link" at lower left.

A smiling Santa Claus in a fur-trimmed red coat and a holly-sprigged cap raises a pewter tankard high and holds a long, thin pipe or quill in his other hand. He stands within a painted arch against a swirling gray-green and ochre background, framed by dark red scrollwork and rosettes. The deep reds and browns give the scene a warm, old-fashioned holiday mood. Signed and dated "G Link '78" at lower right.

This waist-length portrait is painted in the style of the eighteenth century. A dark-haired man with his hair drawn back in a queue wears a navy uniform coat with wide buff lapels and gold buttons, a gold-edged buff waistcoat, and a white ruffled cravat. He turns slightly and meets the viewer's gaze against a plain dark background. Signed "G Link" at lower right.

A seated woman in a white ruffled bonnet tied with a large bow, a broad pale collar, and a black dress holds a pink rose and faces the viewer with a slight smile. A draped curtain with a tassel and part of a chair back set her against a warm brown background. The pose and dress follow nineteenth-century portrait conventions. A very faint signature appears at lower left.

A village scene in Cascais, Portugal, painted in loose, airy washes. Whitewashed houses with clay-tile roofs surround a sunlit yard where red and blue laundry hangs from a propped line, three figures gather at a doorway, and two chickens stand in the foreground. The soft violet sky and pale ground give the scene a quiet, everyday feel. The work is signed and dated "G Link '79" in pencil at lower left with the caption "Cascais, Portugal," placing it among the artist's Portuguese subjects of 1979.

A large red brick house with dormers, chimneys and porches, seen at an angle behind a massive bare tree whose grey trunk and spreading limbs dominate the foreground. Pastel strokes laid over a pale watercolor wash give the bare branches and brick walls a textured, sketch-like quality, and the season appears to be late fall or winter. The title identifies the building as the Link house. The work is signed "G Link" at lower left but undated.

A black-and-white studio portrait of a smiling young woman with dark hair swept back from her forehead and falling in soft curls to her shoulders, catalogued as a photograph of Gretchen Link. The head-and-shoulders pose, plain light background and soft vignette are typical of formal studio portraiture. A faint embossed studio mark appears at lower right of the print, which is mounted in a cream mat.

A tidy red brick Cape Cod style house with a steep grey roof, single dormer and tall exterior chimney, set on a pale lawn with shrubs along its foundation. An evergreen bough reaching in from the upper left frames the composition against a blue sky with drifting clouds. The handling is careful and light, with clean architectural lines softened by watercolor washes. The work is signed and dated "G Link '61" in ink at lower right.

A still life of two red tomatoes, a green bell pepper and a yellow crookneck squash arranged on a white cloth against an olive green background. The paint is applied thickly, with heavy, broken strokes in the cloth and rounded modeling in the vegetables that catches highlights on their skins. The strong reds and greens give the small composition a bold, direct character. The painting is signed "G Link" at lower left and is undated.

A sepia cabinet card portrait of a small girl with long light hair and a bow, wearing a white dress with a ruffled yoke, dark stockings and boots, and leaning against an ornate wicker chair. Her expression is serious, in keeping with studio portraits of the period. The mount carries the photographer's name "Berkeley" and "Staunton, Va." The title identifies the sitter as the mother of a family member known as Nana. The print is faded and scratched at upper right.

A whitewashed round windmill with a dark conical cap and triangular cloth sails rigged on long wooden spars, standing on a stony, grassy rise. Blue colored-pencil hatching behind the mill sets off the white sails, while a path leads to its low door and a small dark dog lies in the grass nearby. The drawing combines crisp ink line with light colored pencil. It is inscribed "Portugal Oct 79" at lower right, dating it to October 1979.

Gretchen Link's earliest sketchbook, a spiral-bound "Monterey" drawing book marked "I" on the cover, opens with a hand-lettered title page reading "ART 34-36" and "Gretchen Hitt." Most pages are pencil, with a few watercolors and ink drawings, and are signed "Gretchen Hitt" or "G.L.H." with dates from 1934 to 1937, most of them from 1935 and 1936. Subjects range from flower studies (jonquils, roses, hibiscus, canna) and architectural exercises such as Ionic and Doric columns to trees, cottages, a sailing ship and a Western saddle. Captioned sketches record Southern California places, including Lytle Creek, Huntington Beach and Huntington Pier, San Antonio Falls and a mountain log cabin labeled "Our Cabin." Portrait and figure work includes informal studies of the artist's mother, quick sketches of cats and chickens, a toddler, and fashion-style drawings of costumed women and dancers from the summer of 1936. Two later additions close the book: "Old Stone Church, Staunton, Va." signed "G Link" in 1976, and a 2011 ballpoint sketch of a bird on a fence post captioned "Card from Bennie."

A spiral-bound travel sketchbook that Gretchen Link titled "Window Sketches 1977-81" on its first page, followed by a handwritten list of the places it covers. Many drawings are labeled as views from hotel windows or balconies. They run roughly in travel order: Spain in 1977 (Seville, Toledo, Granada and the Alhambra), England and Scotland in 1978 (London, Bristol, Salisbury, Windsor, Edinburgh), Cape Cod and Florida, Portugal in 1979 (Cascais and Albufeira), and Ireland in 1980 (Galway, Westport, Sligo, Dublin, Wexford, Bantry, Killarney, Limerick). The 1981 pages cover the American South and New England, with North Carolina, Hilton Head, Savannah, Charleston, Cape Cod and Nantucket. Most pages are pen or marker drawings with colored pencil, among them rooftops, chimneys, church spires, gateways, bridges and coastal views. A few show people, such as Portuguese children and a woman at a window, and some depict personal subjects like "Our Villa" and the Chatham "Our House". Most pages are signed and dated, and a few carry faint mirror-image set-offs of the facing drawings.

A travel sketchbook kept by Gretchen Link from 1982 to 1994, inscribed "G. Link, Staunton, Va." inside the cover and opening with a handwritten list of the years and places it covers. Most pages are signed, captioned and dated pen drawings, many touched with colored pencil, of buildings, rooftops, hotel entrances, staircases and views from hotel windows. The earliest group, from October 1982, records Torremolinos and Ronda in Spain, along with rooftops and robed figures in Tangier. A 1983 trip runs through Amsterdam, a hunting lodge hotel in Germany, the Black Forest, Lucerne, Dijon, Paris, Canterbury and London, followed by Bardstown, Kentucky. In 1984 come Dulles Airport, Folkestone, Buxton, Castleton, Grange-over-Sands, Melrose, Aberfoyle, Glasgow and Blenheim Palace, then Berkeley Springs and Shepherdstown, West Virginia. Later additions include a Coast Guard station at Nags Head (1991) and a Charleston church (1994). A few captions add personal notes, such as "Great food" and "Bought crock here."

Gretchen Link's fourth sketchbook, marked "IV" on the cover, records three trips between 1985 and 1988 in brisk brown or black pen, with occasional colored pencil and marker. The spring 1985 western tour fills the first half: the Figueroa Hotel and Hollywood hills in Los Angeles, boats and palms at Mission Bay in San Diego, the Ko-Pah lookout tower near Jacumba, Lake Havasu, Moqui Lodge at the Grand Canyon, Las Vegas hotels, San Francisco City Hall and Mission San Juan Capistrano. September 1986 pages turn to Massachusetts, with a Gloucester lighthouse, Rockport shops and an autumn house in Great Barrington. June 1988 pages follow a Southwest trip through El Paso, Carlsbad, Albuquerque, Mesa Verde, Cortez, Shiprock and Santa Fe, adding mule deer, animal skulls, pottery and portraits of a tour guide and driver. Many views are drawn from hotel windows. A later page is inscribed "Gretchen Link, 1985, Western tour," and several pages hold faint, unfinished pencil studies.

A travel sketchbook kept by Gretchen Link from 1987 to 1999, opening with a handwritten title page, "Sketches, Gretchen Link," that lists the places visited. Most pages are quick pen drawings, some touched with colored pencil, captioned with place and date, and several are noted as drawn from hotel or motel windows. The book begins in Philadelphia in May 1987 with rooftops, a street lamp and Independence Hall, then moves to Highland, Boston, Jackson, New Hampshire, Quebec and Bar Harbor. Later pages record Nags Head, Berkeley Springs, Etowah Valley, Crystal City, Sandbridge, Tides Lodge in Irvington, and a 1993 visit to Ocracoke with its lighthouse, ferry and umbrella-shaded waterfront tables. The last drawings, from 1998 and 1999, show Kill Devil Hills and Montgomery and Charleston, West Virginia. The pages are not strictly chronological, and among them are pencil studies of a small shaggy dog, sketches of a newborn labeled Baby "Jay" from October 1992, and a scene titled "Nap Time."

A small spiral-bound Strathmore drawing pad mixes travel sketches, figure and animal studies, and practical notes, with dated pages from 1985 to about 2000. Many of the drawings are of the coast or the water: boats tied up at a dock among autumn trees, captioned "Alton Bay" and signed "G. Link" in ink and colored pencil; a row of weathered beach houses behind dune grass labeled "Kitty Hawk"; and a soft study of sea grass and gulls. Other pages hold a farm scene captioned "Demo at Rockport," a shaded sketch of a couple at a terrace table with cats nearby, two studies of an antlered deer, a sleeping dog marked "Cheese," and a portrait labeled "Fred." A design page plans a wreath of eucalyptus, sea oats, shells and yarrow above a sign lettered "Meet me at the Beach." A 1985 gasoline log naming Port Jervis, Sturbridge, Chambersburg and Staunton and a page of gardening notes record everyday concerns.

A spiral-bound Utrecht sketchbook signed "Gretchen Link" on its cover, with dated pages running from February 1987 to 1998. It opens with pencil notes from what appears to be a watercolor class on studying pattern, value and trees, followed by loose monochrome wash exercises of trees, a flower-filled barrel planter, a lake scene and a rose in a jar. Later pages move among pencil, ink, colored pencil, oil pastel and watercolor, drawing houses and porches, a stone tower, a log cabin captioned "Log cabin E Beverly St", basket still lifes, birdhouses and a double portrait. Many pages record the Outer Banks and Virginia shore, captioned Sandbridge, Nags Head and Kill Devil Hills, with beach cottages, dunes and fences. Also included are notes on mat cutting and paint colors, a sketch for a snowman card, and loose inserts: two Nags Head beach sketches, a London fruit stall drawn near Harrods, a magazine page and a Staunton newspaper clipping.

A large Strathmore watercolor pad, bound at the top, holds three finished watercolors between its plain brown covers. The first is a dramatic rural scene: a weathered gambrel-roofed barn and a lattice windmill on a hilltop, with heavy grey and violet storm clouds breaking to yellow light above rust and ochre slopes. The second turns to the coast, showing a sand dune with beach grass, a railed wooden deck, slatted sand fences casting long violet shadows, and a small figure climbing toward the deck. The third is a simple still life of a mottled stoneware jug and a yellow apple set against a loose red wash. Each painting is signed "G Link" at lower left. Faint digits beneath the signature on the still life may read "88," suggesting a date of about 1988, though the reading is uncertain. The back cover carries small handwritten labels, including "S8."

A Winsor & Newton Cotman watercolor pad with "G Link" written on the front cover and a small "S9" label on the back holds five pages of domestic and backyard subjects. The one finished landscape shows a blonde woman in a pale blue dress pinning washing to a line, a wicker basket at her feet, with a blue house behind and a lawn crowded with red and pink flowers, painted in loose, bright washes and signed "G Link". A faint, unfinished pencil drawing of dresses and aprons hanging before a picket fence returns to the laundry theme, and another light pencil outline sets up a still life of flowers, a bowl and fruit on a draped table. A pencil view of a long, low house with shrubs, a birdbath and a curving drive is captioned "FREDS HOUSE". The last painting, a whipped-cream cake heaped with strawberries and blueberries and topped by one candle, is signed "G Link" and captioned "Birthday '01 Boars Head", which dates the book to 2001.

Gretchen Link fills this spiral-bound sketchbook with studies in ink, pencil, red-brown chalk and colored media, with dated pages from 1977 to 1980 and one later drawing from January 1992. Early pages hold still lifes of a bone on a mushroom-like form, a crumpled paper bag signed "G Link 77" and glass bottles and jars signed "G Link 79." A run of figure studies shows what appears to be the same long-haired girl in a sweater and short skirt, standing, kneeling, sitting on the floor, holding pom-poms and perched on a stool by a window. Ink drawings depict the "S M A Mess Hall 1913," dated June '77, and a house captioned "Gibbs Hill, Bishop House," June '80. Other pages show a toddler among toys, a vivid oil pastel bouquet titled "Pauline's Iris" (May '80), folk-art object sketches and a garden with a robed statue. The 1992 page shows stuffed animals and dolls at a holiday tea party.

A summer beach scene in loose, transparent watercolor washes, looking out across pale sand to a blue sea under a soft, cloudy sky, with a low green headland on the horizon at left. Beach umbrellas punctuate the composition: one in faded pink lies tipped over on the sand at left, while a striped blue, red and white umbrella and a yellow one stand upright at right. Small, lightly sketched figures sit beneath and between them, one in a white sun hat, and children wade in the shallow surf beyond. Quick strokes of dune grass frame the foreground, and the figures are suggested with a few touches of color rather than detailed. The painting is signed "G Link" at lower left.

A set of seven small black bust silhouettes by Gretchen Link, each showing a single figure in profile and dressed in fashions that appear to date from the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. Two are mounted on tan paper in round turned wooden frames and form a pair: a man in a tall top hat and a woman in a deep pointed bonnet trimmed with a sprig and tied with a ribbon bow, each marked with a small inked "GL" monogram at lower right. The five unframed sheets show a man with a ribboned queue, a man with a large hair bow and ruffled jabot on an oval sheet, a woman in a frilled mob cap, a young woman with her hair in a looped bun, and a man with swept-back hair and a ruffled shirt frill. The profiles are crisply outlined, and a few use thin reserved lines to mark collars and lapels. Several sheets show water stains and foxing.
